title: A small RPC layer
hints: Write the encoding helpers (id, string, list) and a small reader that tracks its position and an "ok" flag once, and share them between client and server. A message is well formed when the reader never ran out and finished exactly at the end.
Catch `std::invalid_argument` around the handler call in the server, so a bad argument becomes an error reply instead of an exception escaping to the transport.
requirements: Both sides encode and decode the wire format exactly, rejecting malformed messages.
Unknown methods and handler errors become error replies; the server never throws.
Responses are matched by id, late ones are ignored, and timeouts are reported.
Events reach the client in order.
stretch: Run it for real: a named pipe server and a client process, with the length-prefixed framing of lesson 2.03 around each message, the client sending several calls without waiting and handling events on the same connection.
